title: Rule revisability does not guarantee evidence coverage
problem: Owner stated that no rule is sacred and all rules and reviewers require periodic review as knowledge grows. Can a review discover defects if the incumbent rule determines which labels are observable?
failure: Two worlds can share identical accepted labels and decisions but reverse the relative quality of the incumbent and candidate rule. Repeating review on the same admitted region cannot resolve this.
correction: Separate permission to revise from observability. Audit the excluded region with independently determined labels; under fixed finite population and perfect audit assumptions, uniform sampling without replacement attains minimax miss probability C(N-m,d)/C(N,d). Detection is not proof that a replacement rule is superior.
transfer: Predeclare review coverage, preserve rejected evidence and versions, quantify detection power, and evaluate a proposed revision with separate representative evidence. No observed error is not proof of correctness.
limits: Fixed binary truth labels, unit misclassification loss, safe perfect audit of excluded items, known finite sampling frame, equal costs. 2916 label completions, 7638 exact subset checks, six audit-budget boundaries; adaptive minimax extension derived separately. No production, religious-historical, empirical, originality or independent validation claim.
author: TOTO
